overview: Members of the Medford High School building project design team met with community members in a breakout session to discuss climate, energy, and atmospheric design goals. The discussion focused on life cycle cost analyses, HVAC systems, geothermal permitting, and student feedback mechanisms.

items.title: Climate, Energy, and Life Cycle Cost Analysis
items.summary: Paul Garrity asked about materials, battery backups, and 50-year cost escalations, which Martine Dion explained are evaluated through a comprehensive life cycle cost analysis.

items.title: Geothermal Test Well Drilling
items.summary: Matt Rice stated that a geothermal test well funded by a MassCEC grant will be drilled in the coming weeks at no cost to the city.

items.title: Low-Carbon Materials and Red List Standards
items.summary: Martine Dion explained that low-emitting materials and Red List-free products are standard industry options that do not carry premium costs.

items.title: HVAC Selection and Budget Implications
items.summary: Speakers discussed how HVAC choices, including hybrid systems and carport solar panels, are evaluated based on their 50-year total cost of ownership rather than upfront costs alone.

items.title: Student Engagement in School Design
items.summary: Matt Rice described methods used to collect student feedback, including shadow days, dedicated programming meetings, and student-led building tours.

items.title: Site Logistical and Permitting Challenges
items.summary: The design team and attendees discussed challenges with sloped terrain, temporary heating requirements, and Article 97 permitting for drilling under deed-restricted open space.
